item.title: Nishi-Iya Mountain Villages: Life on the Slopes — Guide
item.description: The West Iya Valley (Nishi-Iya) is one of the most remote and atmospheric corners of rural Japan, where tiny villages and farmhouses cling to breathtakingly steep mountain slopes high above the gorges. For centuries, isolated communities here farmed terraced plots on near-vertical ground, developing a distinctive way of life shaped by the mountains. Today you can drive the winding roads between hamlets, see thatched-roof farmhouses (some restored as inns), and take in views over the deep valley.
